title: January 6 Event Record
method: Chronology establishes sequence, not by itself motive, causation, intent, or legal responsibility. Times use official records and identify approximation where appropriate.

events.title: Washington prepares for the electoral count and demonstrations
events.note: Pre-event security and intelligence records provide context for preparations and identified threats.

events.title: The Ellipse rally begins
events.note: The speech and related records should be evaluated in full context; chronology alone does not establish legal responsibility.

events.title: West Front outer security perimeter is breached
events.note: Official congressional materials place the first West Front outer-perimeter breach at approximately 12:53 p.m.

events.title: Congress convenes to count electoral votes
events.note: The Congressional Record documents the joint session and electoral-count proceeding.

events.title: President Trump's Ellipse speech concludes
events.note: The initial West Front outer-perimeter breach preceded the conclusion of the speech; that sequence does not alone resolve questions of influence, intent, planning, or responsibility.

events.title: Arizona electoral votes are challenged
events.note: Congressional records document the objection and the chambers' subsequent votes.

events.title: Capitol Police Chief seeks immediate National Guard assistance
events.note: Later congressional and oversight records document the request and the subsequent approval/deployment process.

events.title: The Capitol building is breached
events.note: Official records document forced entry and the interruption of congressional proceedings; individual criminal responsibility depends on case-specific evidence and adjudication.

events.title: Congressional proceedings are interrupted and protected locations are used
events.note: Government investigative records document the security crisis, evacuation/protection measures, and interruption of the count.

events.title: Law enforcement works to regain control
events.note: The response involved multiple agencies and command structures; later reviews identified planning, intelligence, coordination, and response failures.

events.title: Congress reconvenes and resumes the electoral count
events.note: The Senate rejected the Arizona objection 93–6 and the House rejected it 303–121; the count continued.

events.title: The electoral count is completed
events.note: Congress completed the proceeding and the official Electoral College result was 306 votes for Joseph R. Biden Jr. and 232 for Donald J. Trump.
